Naimiṣāraṇya
(‘wheel-rim forest’)
------------------------------------------
When several ṛṣis or sages appealed to ब्रह्मा to show them an ideal place for the performance of sacrifices and austerities, he is said to have set a wheel rolling and told them that the place where the nemi or the rim of the wheel will drop off, is the most suitable place. Since the nemi fell at this place it came to be known as Naimiṣa (or Naimiśa) or नैमिषारण्य.
It was on the right bank of the river गोमती.
It is now identified with Nīṁsar, about 40 kms. (24 miles) from the railway station Sondilla in Uttar Pradesh.
The पुराणस् mention it as a place where many वेदिच् सच्रिड़िचेस् had been performed. It was also here that many demons had been decimated in a matter of minutes (nimiṣa = minute).
Again, it is here that the famous सूतपुराणिक (Ugraśravas) narrated many incidents and stories of the ancient period, including the Bhārata.
Arjuna had visited this place during his पिल्ग्रिमगे.
Some of the holy places associated with this place are: चक्रतीर्थ, Pañca-प्रयाग, temple of ललिता, Jānakīkuṇḍa; and, temples of शिव and हनुमान्.

naimittika-karma
(‘occasional duties’)
------------------------------------------
Obligatory duties to be performed on special occasions like birth and death in a family are called ‘naimittika-karmas.’ Jāteṣṭi and śrāddha are two examples. Their performance will not produce any special merit, but their non-performance will entail sin.
